records.description: Japan began releasing ALPS-treated water from the Fukushima Daiichi plant on 24 August 2023 under a roughly 30-year plan. records.title: Korean fish farms lose a record 143 billion won to heat in 2024 and face repeat die-offs in 2025 and 2026
records.description: Korea's National Institute of Fisheries Science put 2024 aquaculture losses from extended extreme sea temperatures at 143 billion won, the largest since statistics began, including 25.82 million fish and shellfish dead on South Jeolla farms and a record 17.19 million on South Gyeongsang's south coast. Die-offs recurred in 2025 and again in summer 2026: 360,707 farmed fish had been reported dead nationwide by 3 August, about five times the same point in 2025, and by 4 September 13.533 million had died at 455 farms, with the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries at Serious Level I of its high-water-temperature alert. Response measures include liquid oxygen supply equipment, early harvest and emergency releases, and a South Chungcheong pilot that moves cage fish to a cooler heat refuge. The Korea Meteorological Administration reports marine heatwave days around Korea at 83.3 a year over the past decade against 22.6 on the long-term average.

records.title: Noto Peninsula earthquake lifts the coast by 4 m or more and strands fishing ports
records.description: The 1 January 2024 magnitude 7.5 Noto earthquake raised parts of the peninsula's north coast by as much as 4 m in NASA's account, and a later measurement near Cape Saruyama in Wajima gave 5.2 m, exposing seabed and leaving some ports dry. Damage was confirmed at 60 of 69 fishing ports in Ishikawa, and the Fisheries Agency's 21 March 2024 update listed 20 ports where catch could not be landed, with most ports in Wajima and Suzu considered unusable. By September 2025 the seabed around Wajima port had risen 1.5 to 2 m, boats moored in layers at temporary piers and large vessels used Kanazawa, about 90 km away. Main restoration of the Naoetsu port quay in Niigata was reported complete in March 2025.

records.title: Japanese flying squid has no international catch limit while foreign catches in the Sea of Japan are poorly known
records.description: The North Pacific Fisheries Commission's January 2026 species summary states that the measure then in force for Japanese flying squid sets no catch or effort limits and that the Commission has done no stock assessment, leaving management to domestic rules such as Japan's total allowable catch. A new measure, CMM 2026-11, entered into force on 1 June 2026: it asks members to refrain from expanding the number of authorised vessels until the Commission's Scientific Committee completes a stock assessment, but sets no catch limit. Japan's own assessment says Chinese and North Korean catches are not well known and assumes a Chinese catch of 150,000 tonnes a year over the 2004 to 2020 seasons, except in 2004, 2009 and 2013 when it judged catches to be small, drawing on a 2020 satellite study that counted over 900 Chinese vessels fishing in North Korean waters in 2017.

records.title: Greece commits to end bottom trawling in marine parks by 2026 and all protected areas by 2030
